transcript.text: What's up, brother? What's going on? My
question is what do you look for as far
as going all in on one part of your
business?
>> Honestly, I watch a lot of Steve Jobs
for this stuff. His definition that I
really like, which was like he would ask
his executives all the time. He said,
"What have you said no to lately?"
That's what he would start his
conversation. What have you said no to
lately? And he said that and and talked
to the executives, they're like, "I used
to just like throw them fodder that like
he's like, but those were easy no's."
He's like, "What's something that you
wanted to do in like your core that you
were so excited about that you said no
to? That's what I want to know." Because
that's how dedicated he was to making
sure the one thing that mattered most
happened. This is everyone here's job at
the end of the day is being able to say,
"There is 10 things that I really want
to do and they will all make us more
money."
But they're all of these have
contingencies. Like this will happen if
this happens and this could happen if
this happens. But there's usually a one
domino that if this one doesn't happen,
none of these matter. It's trying to
identify what is that one thing that if
only that thing happened by the end of
the year, the rest of our goals would
either shrink into irrelevance or
accomplish themselves on their own. And
I just spend a lot of time trying to
make sure that I get that one thing
right and then the rest of it kind of
tends to take care of itself.
